detail.longDescription: Hi HN, k8sman is a native lighter-weight Kubernetes IDE. It’s a Flutter GUI on top of a Go backend that works with client-go and your existing kubeconfig. Nothing installed in the cluster and no telemetry whatsoever. Just some of the features I think are unique: - Low footprint (~ 50% RSS compared to Lens on the same cluster) - Inspector panels for 30+ kinds that explain what's wrong (a crash-looping pod shows its exit code, termination message and a link to the previous instance's logs) - Customisable views with a compact query language (status!=Running restarts>3 age<1h), with sortable, resizable and reorderable columns that persist per kind - Streamed logs with searching, pod terminals, alerts, port-forwards that persist across pod restarts, and local shell with kubectl that follows the cluster you look at - Helm history with diffs between revisions, rollbacks and dry-run upgrades - Read-only mode per context (enabled by default for everything that looks like prod) - Integrated with Argo CD, Prometheus, Trivy image scanning (but works just as well without!) Builds for macOS, Windows and Linux. Apache 2.0.
